subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Transform the equation 3x+4y+12=0 into normal form.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what has to be true of p, and what you divide by.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Make the constant positive
steps.margin_note: First mark. Normal form is xcosα + ysinα = p with p POSITIVE, so before dividing, arrange the equation so the number on the right is greater than zero — multiply through by −1 if it is not.
steps.memory_tip: Normal form needs p POSITIVE, so multiply through by −1 if the right side is not.
lines: Normal form is  xcosα + ysinα = p,  p > 0

recall.must_convey: That the equation is arranged with a positive constant on the right before dividing.
accept: normal form needs p positive so fix the sign first
move the constant across and make it positive
multiply by minus one if the right side is negative
p positive ga undali kabatti sign correct cheyyali
arrange it with a positive right hand side

steps.why: p is a DISTANCE from the origin, so it cannot be negative — that requirement is what fixes the signs of cosα and sinα, and with them the quadrant of α.
common_mistakes: Dividing while the right side is still negative, giving a negative p.
Changing the sign of only some terms.

steps.label: Divide and read off
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Divide through by √(a²+b²) so the coefficients square-and-add to 1, then name the angle whose cosine and sine they are.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by √(a²+b²) so the coefficients square-and-add to 1, then name the angle.
lines: We write it as x cosα + y sinα = p
Hence tanα = 4/3, and α lies in Q₃, so α = 180° + Tan⁻¹(4/3)

lines.text: ⇒ x(−3/5) + y(−4/5) = 12/5,  with α = 180° + Tan⁻¹(4/3) in the third quadrant

recall.must_convey: That dividing by √(a²+b²) puts it in normal form x(−3/5) + y(−4/5) = 12/5,  with α = 180° + Tan⁻¹(4/3) in the third quadrant.
accept: divide by the root of a squared plus b squared and read off the angle
the coefficients then square and add to one
write it as x cos alpha plus y sin alpha equals p
root a square plus b square tho divide cheyyali
heard_as: root a squared plus b squared

steps.why: Only after dividing do the coefficients satisfy cos²α + sin²α = 1, which is what lets them be named as a cosine and a sine at all.
common_mistakes: Dividing by a + b instead of √(a² + b²).
Naming an angle in the wrong quadrant for the signs obtained.

insider_note: Normal form needs p > 0, so multiply through by −1 BEFORE dividing; dividing first gives a negative p and earns nothing. Both cosα and sinα then come out negative, which puts α in the third quadrant.
